title: A private directory teardown cannot remove no longer stops it before the site's SMTP rule, network and job records
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation/test/teardown-volumes.test.mjs

S2: Record the exit code, the '# tests', '# pass', '# fail' lines and the result of each case whose name starts with: "a private directory that will not go at first is tried once more after a short wait, and the teardown finishes"; "a private directory that never goes: the steps after it still run, and the teardown fails naming it"; "the site's own network goes with it, and only that one; a network still in use is a teardown that did not finish".
expect: S1 exits 0 with '# fail 0' and '# pass' equal to '# tests' (at least 23).

Every named case is 'ok' (none 'not ok', none '# SKIP'): a directory that will not go at first is tried once more after a short wait and the teardown finishes; one that never goes is reported with rm's reason, steps 4 (subnet SMTP rule), 4b (network) and 5 still run, and the run exits 1 naming what is left instead of torn_down=1; the site's own network still goes and only that one.

selectors.verdict: '!! teardown of <label> did not finish' line instead of TRACY_RESULT torn_down=1

evidence: 05/10/2026, twice: deleting a site whose install had failed stopped at teardown step 3 (bare rm -rf under set -e: 'Directory not empty' on webroot-baseline.git), so its SMTP rule, its <label>_default network and /24 and its private directory all stayed on the host (ledger L14b, reproduced 1/1). Red 6c8278be0 (exit 1 at step 3, no iptables call, network left), fix 57f76e126.
fence: Step 1c still proves the volumes gone before any directory is removed; a path that stays makes the teardown fail loudly after the later steps ran, so running it again finishes the job.

tests: a private directory that will not go at first is tried once more after a short wait, and the teardown finishes
a private directory that never goes: the steps after it still run, and the teardown fails naming it
the site's own network goes with it, and only that one; a network still in use is a teardown that did not finish
